caption: Matthew deliberately depicts Jesus through Psalm 22’s mocked, head-shaken sufferer. The correspondence is strong because the Gospel reuses the psalm.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 22 predict Jesus’s mockers? The psalmist is mocked by people shaking their heads. Matthew describes passers-by doing the same to Jesus.
slides.body: The psalmist is mocked by people shaking their heads. Matthew describes passers-by doing the same to Jesus.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 22 predict Jesus’s mockers?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 22:7: All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads.
slides.body: All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads.
slides.heading: Ps 22:7

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Matt 27:39–44, BSB: Those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads … In the same way, the chief priests, scribes, and elders mocked Him.
slides.body: Those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads … In the same way, the chief priests, scribes, and elders mocked Him.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Matt 27:39–44

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The match is deliberate Matthew uses more Psalm 22 language throughout the scene. Jesus is presented as its suffering figure.
slides.body: Matthew uses more Psalm 22 language throughout the scene. Jesus is presented as its suffering figure.
slides.heading: The match is deliberate

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Matthew knows the psalm The original is a sufferer’s present prayer. Literary reuse explains why Matthew’s later account matches it so closely.
